title: Payment taps → Kassa
settingsHint: Log Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Pay, Alipay and WeChat Pay
intro: Your phone sends each payment to Kassa. Kassa logs the spend and answers with one line (budget left, fee or DCC warning) that your phone shows as a notification.
limits: Taps in shops: needs iOS 17 or later and a card in Apple Wallet. The amount may be a pre-authorisation that settles later. It only logs spending: it never approves or blocks a payment. A tap made offline is not sent again.
endpointFooter: Paste this as the URL of “Get Contents of URL”.
endpointUnknown: Set EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL to show the full address; the path is /api/capture/shortcut on your Kassa server.
tokenFooter: One token per iPhone. Anyone with the token can add spending to your log, nothing else. Revoke it below if it leaks.
tokenOnce: Copy it now: Kassa shows this token only once.

quick.title: Quick setup
quick.after: Your link is copied. In Shortcuts tap Add Shortcut and paste it when asked. Then Automation → + → Transaction → pick your Wallet cards → Run Immediately → Next → Log to Kassa.
quick.footer: iOS lets no app create the automation itself, so that last step is yours. Then pay once and use “Test it live” above.
quick.needToken: Create a token above first: the Shortcut asks for a link with it.
quick.copyFailed: Could not copy the link. Copy it by hand instead.

steps.1: Create a token above and copy the header value.
steps.2: Open Shortcuts → Automation → + → Transaction. Pick your Wallet cards, choose Run Immediately, then Next → New Blank Automation.
steps.3: Add “Get Contents of URL”. URL: the endpoint above. Method: POST. Headers: Authorization = Bearer <token>. Request Body: JSON with merchant = Shortcut Input › Merchant, amount = Shortcut Input › Amount, card = Shortcut Input › Card or Pass.
steps.4: Add “Get Dictionary Value”: Value for key nudge in Contents of URL.
steps.5: Add “Show Notification” with the Dictionary Value.
steps.6: Pay with Apple Pay. A Kassa line appears a moment later and the spend is in Activity.

revokeBody: The Shortcut stops logging taps at once. Create a new token to connect it again.

online.title: Online and in-app Apple Pay
online.why: Apple's Transaction trigger only runs for taps at a payment terminal. Apple Pay in Safari or inside an app never reaches it, so Kassa reads the SMS your bank sends for each card payment instead. Chinese bank SMS (尾号…消费…元) work the same way.
online.footer: Only messages you choose are sent. Kassa ignores texts it cannot read as a payment.

steps.1: Open Shortcuts → Automation → + → Message. Message Contains: a word every payment SMS from your bank has, or pick your bank as the Sender. Choose Run Immediately.
steps.2: Add “Get Contents of URL” with the same URL, method and Authorization header as above. Request Body: JSON with text = Shortcut Input › Content and app = Shortcut Input › Sender.
steps.3: Add “Get Dictionary Value” for nudge, then “Show Notification”, as above.
steps.4: Pay online with Apple Pay. When the bank SMS arrives, the spend is in Activity.

android.title: Set up on Android
android.limits: Works with Google Wallet, Samsung Wallet, Alipay, WeChat Pay and your bank's app: anything that shows a notification for a payment, in shops, online or in apps. It only logs spending: it never approves or blocks a payment.
android.footer: Android lets an automation app read notifications; iOS does not, which is why iPhone uses Shortcuts instead.

steps.1: Create a token above and copy the header value.
steps.2: Install an automation app such as MacroDroid or Tasker. New macro → trigger “Notification received” → pick Google Wallet, Samsung Wallet, Alipay, WeChat and your bank app.
steps.3: Allow the app notification access when Android asks.
steps.4: Action “HTTP request”: POST to the endpoint above, header Authorization = Bearer <token>, content type application/json, with the body below.
steps.5: Optional: save the response and show its nudge field as a notification.
steps.6: Pay with your phone. A moment later the spend is in Activity.

test.title: Test your Shortcut
test.openHint: Pay once with Apple Pay and see exactly what reached Kassa.
test.intro: This test only trusts what the server receives. Press Start, then pay with Apple Pay on your iPhone. Every request your Shortcut makes from now on is listed below, refused ones too, with what it carried.
test.keysFooter: A key is the token or link inside your Shortcut. A request with a key Kassa has never seen (a typo, or another server) cannot be shown here.
test.noKey: You have no active key, so your Shortcut cannot reach Kassa. Create one first.
test.oldServer: This server is too old for the live test. Update the server first.
test.before: Have your iPhone ready, with the automation set to Run Immediately.
test.payNow: Now pay with Apple Pay at a terminal (a small purchase is enough). Online and in-app Apple Pay do not run the Transaction automation.

state.waiting: Nothing has reached Kassa since you pressed Start.
state.manualOnly: Your Shortcut reached Kassa, but without a payment (it was run by hand). That proves the link and key, not the Apple Pay trigger. Now pay with Apple Pay.
state.notShortcuts: A purchase arrived, but from “{{client}}”, not from the Shortcuts app. The automation on your iPhone is not proven.
state.confirm: A purchase reached Kassa from your Shortcut and was logged. Two checks only you can make:
state.wrongAmount: Logged, but with the wrong amount: in the automation, Amount must be Shortcut Input › Amount (not a number you typed).
state.noNotification: Logging works, but your iPhone shows nothing. Add “Get Dictionary Value” (key nudge, from Contents of URL) and then “Show Notification” with the Dictionary Value.
state.noNotificationAction: Logging works, but your iPhone shows nothing. In the “Log Payment in Kassa” action, turn Show Notification on.
state.passed: Working: a real Apple Pay purchase went from your iPhone to Kassa, was logged with the right amount, and your iPhone showed Kassa's reply.

test.askAmount: Is this your purchase, with the right amount?
test.askNotification: Did your iPhone show a notification “{{title}}”?
test.tryAgain: Fix it in the Shortcuts app, then pay again. This list updates by itself.

nothing.title: Still nothing. The usual reasons:
nothing.1: The automation is set to “Run After Confirmation”: set it to Run Immediately.
nothing.2: The card you paid with is not selected under Card in the automation.
nothing.3: The payment was online or in an app: only taps at a terminal run the Transaction trigger.
nothing.4: The Shortcut sends to another address: compare its URL with the one above.
nothing.5: The key in the Shortcut has a typo: create a new key and paste the link again.

test.logFooter: Read from the server. ✓ = the field arrived, ✗ = it did not.
test.scriptClient: This request came from a browser or a script, not from the Shortcuts app.

attempt.noAmount: Arrived without an amount: set Amount to Shortcut Input › Amount
attempt.noMerchant: Arrived without a merchant: set Merchant to Shortcut Input › Merchant
attempt.amountUnreadable: Arrived, but Kassa could not read the amount
attempt.textUnreadable: Message arrived, but Kassa could not read a payment in it
attempt.revokedKey: Refused: the Shortcut uses a key you revoked. Put the new link in it.
attempt.badBody: Refused: {{problem}}. Request Body must be JSON.

voice.title: Ask Kassa by voice
voice.intro: A Shortcut you start with “Hey Siri, Ask Kassa”: you speak, Kassa's AI hears the recording and answers aloud. Ask what you spent or what is due, say “coffee 1,200 forints” to log a purchase, or “send 15 euro to Anna” to draft a payment to one of your recipients.
voice.footer: It never pays by itself: a payment it drafts opens the order page, and only your passkey there sends it. The link holds your Shortcut key: paste it only into Shortcuts.
voice.needToken: Create a token above first: the voice link uses it.

steps.2: Add “Record Audio”: Start Recording Immediately, Finish Recording On Tap.
steps.3: Add “Base64 Encode” with the Recorded Audio.
steps.4: Add “Get Contents of URL”: paste the voice link as the URL. Tap ›: Method POST, Request Body JSON, Text fields audio = Base64 Encoded and format = m4a.
steps.5: Add “Get Dictionary Value”: Value for key reply in Contents of URL.
steps.6: Add “Speak Text” (or “Show Result”) with the Dictionary Value. Then say “Hey Siri, Ask Kassa”.
steps.7: Add “Get Dictionary Value”: Value for key approveUrl in Contents of URL. Then “If” Dictionary Value has any value: “Open URLs” with it, and approve the payment with your passkey on that page.

voice.after: Your voice link is copied. In Shortcuts tap Add Shortcut and paste it when asked. Then say “Hey Siri, Ask Kassa”. A payment you ask for opens its order page: approve it there with your passkey.
